scope: Independent reassessment of the fixed 55 pre-existing no-defensible-ucr-match exceptions; first-stage history and other assessment/QC queues remain separate.

baseline_queue.selection: Baseline canonical recordStatus=exception and exception.type=no-defensible-ucr-match, excluding every case ID in baseline stage2-ucr-assessment.json cases; sorted by baseline normalized production_order.

prior_exception.reason: The programme integrates sustained English proficiency, English phonetics, syntax, historical and world English linguistics, British and American literary history, specialist research and a required thesis. UCR has literature, stylistics, rhetoric and media courses taught in English, but lacks dedicated English-language proficiency and phonology/syntax teaching and the multi-period English literature and linguistics sequence. Filling a 24-course closest match with general literature, history, art and media courses would misrepresent those gaps as English Studies training.
prior_exception.curriculumContext: The public 2027–2028, 2028–2029 and 2029–2030 year-specific pages are provisional prospective-student pathways. The year-three comparison instantiates the non-abroad option, preserving its actual free electives and compulsory thesis.
prior_exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Checked the current GitHub main data/reference/ucr_courses_enriched.xlsx (151 course rows), including profiles, descriptions, prerequisites and planned semester offerings. MCCLITR111/112/211/212/311/312 support general literary analysis and narrative; MCCCOMM111/211/213/311/312 support rhetoric, stylistics and communication; MCCMEDI211 treats American media and HCBCOGN312 psycholinguistics. These are meaningful adjacent studies, but the workbook has no sequence in English phonetics, phonology, syntax, historical English, English language proficiency or period-specific British and American literature. The nearest courses cannot sustain a defensible 24-course English Language and Culture closest match.

interest_assessment.core_coverage_limitation: Core ownership records the closest related literary/cultural response; it does not assert complete coverage of English linguistic/proficiency or region-specific requirements.

candidates.label: English structural, historical and global linguistics
candidates.assessment: Stylistics gives linguistic text analysis and Psycholinguistics gives experimental language processing after HCBGATE102. Neither supplies a cumulative English phonetics/phonology, syntax, historical-language or world-English sociolinguistics curriculum; a complete second direction would require unrelated cognitive/biological filler.

candidates.label: Advanced English proficiency and language development
candidates.assessment: Rhetoric and stylistics support expression and interpretation, but the workbook offers no dedicated advanced English acquisition/proficiency sequence. Teaching in English does not establish that curriculum.

candidates.label: English in science, politics and business
candidates.assessment: The official statement identifies domains where English is used. It does not establish science, politics and business together as a coherent bachelor direction or authorize three unrelated disciplinary additions.

candidates.label: English learning and secondary-school education
candidates.assessment: Rhetoric in Action is primarily Dutch interaction with primary pupils; Psycholinguistics, lifespan development and brain/behaviour supply particular learner/language contributions. The workbook lacks sustained English-learning didactics, secondary classroom curriculum/assessment and pedagogy. A full second programme cannot be grounded in the actual descriptions; professional qualification alone is not the reason.

findings: Historical judgment rejected broader literary/cultural study because it did not reproduce English-specific training; this applied a stricter full-disciplinary-substitution test than the current related-fields contract.
Current exact-target route made explicit without substituting American Studies or changing any external component.
Removed possible stylistics/pragmatics alignment: without adequate component-level support it remains unmatched.
cp-000043.academic_assessment: Study literary form, stylistics, rhetoric and film alongside American cultural representation and source-based modern history. Social theory and the philosophy of emotion support specific analyses of identity, power and responses to fiction; English phonology, syntax, proficiency training and the full British literary-period sequence remain gaps.
limitations: Radboud combines English proficiency, linguistics and sustained British/American literary study with independent research. This UCR programme approaches literary and cultural questions through literature, rhetoric, media and history. It provides related fields rather than the full English Language and Culture curriculum: dedicated English proficiency, phonetics, phonology, syntax and historical-English study are absent, and its British literary-period coverage is less extensive.
External year pages are indicative 2027–2030 prospectus information, not a finalized Fall 2026 external-cohort schedule.
Workbook availability is planned, not guaranteed future delivery.

prior_exception.reason: French Language and Culture combines a four-course French proficiency progression through C1 with study of French-language structure, French–Dutch translation and creative writing, francophone literature and culture, a required period studying at a francophone university and a discipline-specific thesis. UCR has a substantial humanities, media, history and communication offer, but no French language course, francophone literary sequence, French linguistics or translation training. A 24-course selection of general culture and communication courses would be a valid different humanities curriculum but not a defensible closest response to this explicitly French-language programme; it would obscure the central language and region-specific requirements.
prior_exception.curriculumContext: The currently published public year pages establish a 180-EC illustrative pathway. The required study abroad is 15 EC of the major and is not added to the separate 30-EC free elective space. Year-two Faculty of Arts minors are restricted choice, not six invented mandatory French modules.
prior_exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Checked the current GitHub main enriched UCR workbook (151 course rows), including course profiles, prerequisites and planned terms. The literature sequence MCCLITR111/112/211/212/311/312, communication sequence MCCCOMM111/211/213/311/312, media studies MCCMEDI111/112/211/311/312, history and art courses, and HCBCOGN312 Psycholinguistics provide substantial adjacent humanities and general language-analysis material. MCCCOMM112 teaches Dutch, not French. None teaches French proficiency, French linguistics, French–Dutch translation or a focused sequence in francophone literature and culture. The large adjacent cluster cannot supply the missing French-language core of a defensible 24-course closest match.

candidates.label: French linguistics and advanced language acquisition
candidates.assessment: Psycholinguistics after HCBGATE102 and stylistic analysis offer limited cognitive/textual contributions. The workbook has no French proficiency, French structural/historical linguistics, acquisition progression or sustained multilingualism curriculum. General neuroscience and psychology cannot substitute for these defining subjects.

candidates.label: French–Dutch legal and administrative translation
candidates.assessment: Dutch and courses in EU, public international, constitutional or private law provide discrete language/domain contributions. No French or translation method exists in the workbook; a predominantly law curriculum would not implement French–Dutch legal/administrative translation. The failure concerns academic coherence/content, not professional certification.

interest_assessment.distinctness_assessment: Literature/film, art and cultural history already form the accepted concept. More narrowly relabelled cultural candidates lack an independently evidenced set of four substantive course changes. The France/Europe/international-institutions strand has two specific courses; inflating it to a full second political curriculum would extend the target evidence beyond the demonstrated interest.

findings: Historical rejection required French-language/region-specific reproduction even for a related-fields response. A complete cultural-methods programme is defensible under the current contract, with regional and language limitations explicit.
Named French direction (Frans) within Romance Languages and Cultures is now explicit; no Spanish route or generic degree substituted.
Stale year-three prospectus label corrected to 2029–2030 after current official-page retrieval; all settled external components and weights remain unchanged.
Potential Contemporary Literary Field/advanced-literary-theory alignment rejected: the external title alone does not establish a sufficiently precise curricular relationship.
cp-000046.academic_assessment: Study literary and visual expression through text analysis, film, art and museums, alongside cultural history and qualitative social inquiry. Two politics courses examine European and international institutions. This related-fields programme develops cultural interpretation; it provides neither French proficiency and translation nor a sustained francophone regional curriculum.
limitations: Radboud combines French proficiency, linguistics and francophone literature/culture with translation, required francophone-university study and a thesis. This UCR programme studies related literary, visual and historical questions through literature, film, art, history and social inquiry, with European/international institutional contributions. It does not provide French proficiency, French–Dutch translation, required francophone immersion or a sustained francophone regional curriculum.
Public external year pages are provisional prospectus information, not a finalized Fall 2026 external timetable.
Future UCR delivery uses planned workbook availability.

cp-000050.programme: Classics (Greek and Latin Language and Culture) — Radboud

prior_exception.reason: The Greek and Latin grammar, translation, linguistics and original-text literature sequence is integral to Classics across all three years. UCR offers Greek archaeology, ancient democracy and world mythology, but no ancient Greek or Latin language teaching or sustained primary-text sequence. A 24-course UCR programme built around adjacent cultural-history courses would conceal this defining gap rather than constitute a defensible closest match.
prior_exception.curriculumContext: Radboud's current prospective pages are explicitly indicative: year one 2027–2028, year two 2028–2029 and year three 2029–2030. The 180-EC domestic pathway retains restricted year-two Faculty of Arts minors and 30 EC genuine year-three free space. It does not claim a guaranteed Fall 2026-entry timetable. The prior UCR no-match assessment, dated 2026-09-25, remains pending independent stage-two reassessment.
prior_exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Checked all 151 course rows in the current GitHub main data/reference/ucr_courses_enriched.xlsx, including names, outlines/profiles, topics, methods, planned semesters and prerequisites. MCCHEAM213 Greek Archaeology, MCCHEAM315 Heritage & Ancient Democracy, MCCLITR211 World Myth & Literature and MCCHEAM112 Introduction to World Archaeology address portions of ancient material culture and literary themes. No Greek or Latin grammar, translation, original-language text, classical philology or sustained Classics language sequence is available, so these complementary courses cannot anchor a defensible 24-course closest-match programme.

candidates.label: Antiquity, democracy and the politics of the present
candidates.assessment: The target explicitly connects antiquity to later society. A distinct law, politics and history route is coherent and feasible, and differs from the closest route by twelve courses / 90 EC in each direction.

candidates.label: Greek and Latin language, philology and original-text study
candidates.assessment: UCR has rhetoric, stylistics and translated classical literature but no ancient Greek or Latin acquisition, classical linguistics, translation or cumulative original-text sequence.

candidates.label: Teaching Greek and Latin in secondary school
candidates.assessment: The workbook lacks the necessary Greek/Latin subject preparation and classics didactics. The rejection rests on academic content rather than professional qualification alone.

findings: The historic judgment treated the absence of Greek and Latin as barring every complete response; the current contract permits an explicitly related-fields programme when every course has a concrete contribution and the disciplinary gap remains visible.
A second, independently evidenced route on antiquity’s political and legal reception is substantively distinct rather than a relabelling of the closest programme.
The exact domestic third-year comparator route and all 180 EC were preserved after current official-source verification.
cp-000050.academic_assessment: Two related-fields programmes are defensible. The closest route combines translated classical literature and myth, rhetoric, ancient philosophy, archaeology, imperial history, art and reception. The second studies how ancient democracy, citizenship and empire shaped later political and legal orders. Neither is represented as a Greek-and-Latin language or philology curriculum.

verification.pairwise_distinctness: 12 courses / 90 EC unique to each alternative; passed

limitations: UCR does not teach ancient Greek or Latin, classical linguistics, translation or a sustained original-text sequence. The alternatives are related routes, not full substitutes for Radboud Classics.
The Radboud year pages are indicative 2027–2030 prospectus information rather than a finalized Fall 2026 external timetable.
Workbook availability is planned, not guaranteed future delivery.

prior_exception.reason: Radboud’s Islam, Politiek en Samenleving specialisation is defined by compulsory academic study of Islam’s history, prophetic sources, sacred texts, Islamic thought, lived religion, transnational Muslim communities and Islamic theology. The UCR course catalogue contains no Islam or religious-studies sequence, no Islamic theology or Qur’an-based textual training, and no Arabic. A 24-course schedule assembled from politics, sociology, history, law and philosophy would have substantial general social-science content but would omit the target’s defining field. Presenting that schedule as a closest UCR alternative would misstate what UCR teaches.
prior_exception.curriculumContext: The formal 2026–27 OER establishes the exact 180-EC route and the restricted module requirement, resolving the public prospectus’s ambiguous placement of the 30-EC free space. The selected no-Arabic route and two first-listed modules are formal neutral selections, not a match-optimising choice. A completed external reconstruction is preserved even though no academically defensible UCR programme is proposed.
prior_exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Read all 151 records in the current GitHub main data/reference/ucr_courses_enriched.xlsx, including course names, description2, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, planned availability and prerequisites. GOSPOLI112 Foundations of Comparative Politics, GOSSOCI111 Introduction to Sociology, GOSLAWJ213 Comparative Constitutional Law, GOSPHIL212 Ethics and GOSSOCI212 Qualitative Research Methodology could address politics, rights and research methods. MCCHEAM212 Renaissance Italy & Global Mediterranean mentions Islamic courts in a visual-cultural context, and MCCLITR211 World Myth & Literature refers to Arabic literary traditions as one comparative topic. Neither teaches Islam as a disciplinary object or Arabic-language textual analysis. There is no course in Qur’anic sources, Islamic thought, theology or Muslim lived religion; adjacent historical and political courses cannot constitute a 24-course closest-match degree to this specialisation.

interest_assessment.core_coverage_limitation: The related-fields route studies belief, religious expression and public-life questions through literature, philosophy, heritage, law, sociology, psychology and politics. Its Islamic and Arabic-cultural encounters are limited and do not establish Islam, Arabic, theology or sacred-text training.

candidates.label: Arabic, Islamic sources and theology
candidates.assessment: The workbook contains no Arabic acquisition, Qur’anic or other Islamic source-language interpretation, Islamic intellectual-history sequence or Islamic theology.

candidates.label: Religion, climate and environmental justice
candidates.assessment: UCR has coherent sustainability and environmental-justice study, but no religion-and-climate or spiritual-ecology content sufficient to organise 23 non-PPD courses without changing the object of study.

candidates.label: Religion and healthcare
candidates.assessment: Ethics, psychology and public health offer adjacent material, but the workbook lacks religious meanings of care, ritual in healthcare and psychology of religion.

findings: The previous judgment correctly identified the missing Islam and Religious Studies core but applied that gap as a bar to any complete related-fields response.

The independently quality-controlled Religious Studies model transfers to this target only with tighter wording: the programme studies belief and public-life questions and contains two limited Islamic/Arabic-cultural encounters; it does not claim Islam expertise.
The adopted 2026–2027 OER route, neutral restricted-module choices and complete 180-EC comparator were preserved.
cp-000055.academic_assessment: The programme combines myth, literature, philosophy and visual heritage with law, sociology, psychology, politics and media to study belief, religious expression, migration, rights, identity and conflict. Two courses provide limited encounters with Islamic courts and Arabic literary traditions. Islam, Arabic, Islamic theology, sacred texts and religion-specific methods remain explicit gaps.
limitations: UCR does not offer sustained Islam, Arabic, Islamic theology, Qur’anic/source interpretation, lived-religion or religion-specific methods. The programme is a related-fields response, not an Islam or Religious Studies curriculum.
The selected Religion and Care and Worldviews, Nature and Climate modules are neutral formal choices within the adopted route; UCR courses are not used to imitate their religion-specific content.
Workbook availability is planned, not guaranteed future delivery.
